comments.author: @malagasylisa1680
comments.text:
I live in Madagascar (moved here in 2017 from the States). Only some of the Malagasy tribes celebrate famadiahana (FA-ma-DEE-ha-na), moving of the bones, and it’s for male and female ancestors. I have attended several, but I stay away from the bones.
Your mispronunciation of so many words (e.g.Jirama, JEER-ah-ma, Antandroy AHN-tan-DROO-ee) makes me think that you have never set foot on the island. The title of this video, “Why Malagasy Women Never Buy Makeup,” is bizarre. Gasy women are like women everywhere, we do our hair, nails, and makeup. Power outages in Tana have no impact on the rest of the country. Here in Mahajanga, where I live, our power has been far more reliable than in Tana, but when last year’s coup took place, we were all on the same side — getting rid of Rajoelina (rah-JWEL-na). I’ve never heard of a grandfather eating the foreskin — that’s for grandmothers — and circumcisions are done every single year, during May and June, by each private family . Each ceremony lasts three days.

In Madagascar, the letter o sounds like oo, so The Rova (queen’s castle) sounds like ROO-vah. 

Omg, you are mispronouncing SO many words! Merina is MARE-nah, not ma-REE-na. Razana is RAH-za-na.

Lemurs are the best! 

MAMY villages are installing solar farms. I used to live in Mahambo (rural, no electricity or running water) but with their new solar farm, almost all Mahambo families now have access to electricity and this is growing around the island.

I live a simpler life here, and even with the annual cyclones, endemic corruption, undrinkable tap water, and iffy electricity, I much prefer my life here than anywhere in the u.s.

There is no need to buy imported bread, since there are excellent local bakeries here.

I speak no French. My broken Malagasy works well enough, and a lot of people here speak some English.

There ARE pensions here, by the way. There is so much about this magical country that you missed… sigh.

Only a few tribes force the death or separation of twins. I have taught twins and have a few twin friends. I live in the Sakalava Boeny region.
